title: MAGIC ENGLISH GRADE 6 — WORLD 2: A2+ TO B1 BRIDGE
description: A high-volume bridge world designed to move Grade 6 learners from confident A2+ communication toward independent B1 English through richer vocabulary, connected speech, longer texts, multi-speaker listening, sustained conversation, practical writing and realistic problem-solving.

targets.active_vocabulary: 1000+ words, collocations, phrasal verbs and functional expressions
targets.listening: 7–9 minutes, including natural-speed multi-speaker conversations and announcements
targets.speaking: 8–10 minutes of sustained interaction, explanation and role-play
targets.writing: 220–260 words with paragraph structure, linking and clear purpose
grammar: Past Perfect introduction and controlled use
Future forms: will, going to and Present Continuous
Modal verbs for obligation, advice, possibility and deduction
First Conditional and Second Conditional foundations
Gerunds and infinitives in common patterns
Linking words, clauses and paragraph cohesion

missions.title: Vocabulary Engine — Words That Work Together
missions.focus: collocations, word families, phrasal verbs and functional phrases
missions.challenge: Use new words naturally in complete sentences instead of isolated memorization.

missions.title: Present Perfect vs Past Simple — Time Detective
missions.focus: finished time, life experience, recent events, ever/never, already/yet/just
missions.challenge: Choose the tense from meaning and time reference, then explain the choice.

missions.title: Story Control — Past, Past Continuous & Past Perfect
missions.focus: narrative sequence, background actions and earlier events
missions.challenge: Rebuild a mixed-up story and retell it using accurate narrative tenses.

missions.title: Future Mission — Plans, Predictions & Decisions
missions.focus: will, going to, Present Continuous and spontaneous decisions
missions.challenge: Discuss plans, predictions and decisions while selecting the most natural future form.

missions.title: Modal Power — Rules, Advice, Possibility & Deduction
missions.focus: must, have to, should, may, might, could, must be and can't be
missions.challenge: Interpret what a speaker means from context and degree of certainty.

missions.title: Conditional Lab — Real Choices & Possible Worlds
missions.focus: zero/first conditional review and second conditional foundation
missions.challenge: Solve realistic situations using conditions, consequences and hypothetical ideas.

missions.title: Sentence Builder — Add Detail Without Losing Clarity
missions.focus: relative clauses, conjunctions, dependent clauses and sentence expansion
missions.challenge: Transform short sentences into connected B1-style sentences without creating confusion.

missions.title: People & Relationships — Describe, Compare & Understand
missions.focus: personality, relationships, emotions, behavior and social situations
missions.challenge: Describe people precisely and support observations with reasons and examples.

missions.title: Technology & Media — Information Everywhere
missions.focus: devices, apps, online behavior, media, information and digital communication
missions.challenge: Explain how technology affects everyday life and distinguish fact from personal opinion.

missions.title: B1 Conversation Lab — Ten Minutes Together
missions.focus: questions, follow-up questions, clarification, turn-taking and extended answers
missions.challenge: Maintain a natural 8–10 minute conversation without relying on one-word answers.

missions.title: Reading Explorer — The Unexpected Opportunity
missions.focus: main idea, supporting detail, inference, vocabulary in context and sequencing
missions.challenge: Read a 750–900 word story/article and justify answers with evidence from the text.

missions.title: Listening Lab — Four Voices, One Situation
missions.focus: speaker identification, key details, attitude, paraphrase and natural connected speech
missions.challenge: Follow several speakers at natural speed and reconstruct the important information.

missions.title: Writing Lab — One Strong Paragraph Becomes Three
missions.focus: topic sentences, supporting details, examples, connectors and conclusions
missions.challenge: Write 220–260 words with clear paragraph organization and controlled grammar.

missions.title: Dialogue Builder — Say It Naturally
missions.focus: functional language, polite requests, clarification, agreement and disagreement
missions.challenge: Turn formal textbook phrases into natural everyday dialogue while keeping the meaning.

missions.title: Travel Mission — Booking, Changes & Problems
missions.focus: tickets, reservations, hotels, delays, changes, directions and service requests
missions.challenge: Complete a multi-step travel simulation when the original plan changes unexpectedly.

missions.title: Health & Public Services — Explain the Problem
missions.focus: symptoms, appointments, pharmacy language, forms, instructions and polite questions
missions.challenge: Explain a problem clearly, understand instructions and ask useful follow-up questions.

missions.title: Opinion Lab — Give Reasons, Examples & Alternatives
missions.focus: opinions, reasons, examples, contrast, agreement and respectful disagreement
missions.challenge: Give a structured opinion and respond to another viewpoint using connected English.

missions.title: Communication Repair — When English Goes Wrong
missions.focus: clarification, repetition, paraphrasing, checking understanding and repair strategies
missions.challenge: Keep a conversation moving even when a word, instruction or message is misunderstood.

missions.title: A2+ → B1 Integrated Skills Marathon
missions.focus: vocabulary, grammar, reading, listening, speaking and writing under time pressure
missions.challenge: Complete a connected multi-stage mission where every answer feeds the next task.

missions.title: WORLD 2 MASTER QUEST — B1 BRIDGE
missions.focus: full-world mastery and independent communication
missions.challenge: Complete a final integrated scenario combining vocabulary, grammar, reading, listening, conversation, writing, problem solving and real-world communication.

assessment.vocabulary: 1000+ active items with collocations, phrasal verbs and functional language
assessment.grammar: mixed-context accuracy rather than isolated rule recall
assessment.reading: 750–900 word text with inference and evidence questions
assessment.mastery: integrated final mission requiring independent language production
